title: dedicated-capacity-weekly-prep-maya-patel-2026-03-10
content:
Weekly prep notes for dedicated capacity sync (10 Mar 2026)
Owner: Maya Patel
Pulling together numbers + asks for Friday sync with Ryan + Jenna. Draft/notes to self – will clean before drop-in.

Context
- Recent spike in enterprise inference usage (two customers migrated from self-host to Dedicated in Feb). Observed sustained tail that increases 95th pct utilization by ~12% across east/us region.
- Current reserved pool (global): 240 GPUs (A100 equivalent). Utilization this week: 62% average, 88% 95th pct during peak window (15:00-18:00 PT).
- Burst / autoscale capacity currently allowed: +40 GPUs per region (burst from shared pool). We hit burst cap twice last week -> observed 300–420s cold-start latency for new allocs.

Agenda (for sync)
1) Quick numbers (2 mins) – current reserved, utilization, recent anomalies.
2) Forecast + ask (10 mins) – 30/90-day forecast and reservation ask for next quarter.
3) Autoscaling tuning (10 mins) – policy changes to reduce cold-start penalty and cost controls.
4) Risk & rollout plan (5 mins) – canary steps for increasing reservations and mitigation if usage retracts.
5) Action items + owners (3 mins).

Key metrics to present
- Reserved GPUs: 240 A100-eq (global).
- Active clusters: 12 (3 regions), avg cluster size 20 GPUs.
- Weekly growth rate (7d): ~9%. 30d growth: ~28% (driven by two onboarding customers).
- Peak 95th pct utilization (east/us): 88% last Tue 2026-03-03.
- Average cold-start time for burst alloc: 350s (median 260s) – unacceptable for low-latency SLAs.

30 / 90 day forecast (back-of-envelope)
- Baseline scenario (no new big customers): continued organic growth 8%/month -> need +20 GPUs reserved by 2026-04-15.
- Mid scenario (1 medium customer onboard + organic): growth 20%/month -> need +60 GPUs by 2026-04-01 and +140 GPUs by 2026-06-01.
- Upside (2 large customers onboard): +120 GPUs by 2026-04-01.

Recommendation (ask for Friday)
- Request incremental reservation: +60 A100-eq GPUs across east/us + west/us (split 40 east, 20 west) to cover mid scenario through April.
- Temporary increase burst cap to +80 GPUs per region for next 6 weeks while we stabilize autoscaling prewarm pipeline.
- Allocate budget estimate: ~60 GPUs * $2.4/hr equivalent reserved rate -> rough monthly commit delta ~$103,680 (calculation: 60 * 24 * 30 * 2.4). Note: we have discounts at scale – confirm with finance.

Autoscaling / operational changes to propose
- Prewarm pools: maintain a small warm pool of prewarmed containers on 30% of anticipated burst capacity (target 24 GPUs prewarmed in east). Aim to reduce cold-starts to <60s.
- Improve reuse by tagging heavy-tenancy customers to colocate with warm pools (reduce fragmentation).
- Update autoscale policy thresholds: lower scale-out threshold to 75% P95 queue depth for model-serving routes with <200ms latency requirements. Add cooldown 90s.
- Optimize instance startup: vendor kernel + image layering audit (see infra PR) to shave 40–60s.

Risks / open questions
- If growth reverses after reservation commit, we carry excess reserved spend – can we convert some reservation to convertible term or reassign to Hosted customers? (ask finance/legal).
- H100 availability / pricing: if customers request H100 variants, reservation delta/cost will change. Do we need separate SKU forecast?
- Can we get temporary capacity from cloud partner for 2–4 week buffer if we miss ramp? (Ryan to confirm procurement options).

Action items (owners + rough due dates)
- Maya: finalize slides + numbers for Friday sync (2026-03-11 EOD).
- Ryan Wood: confirm procurement / partner temporary capacity options and pricing (2026-03-12).
- Jenna Wu: update autoscaling RFC with proposed thresholds + cooldowns; start prewarm pool runbook draft (2026-03-15).
- Liam Chen: run cost sensitivity matrix for 3 reservation sizes (30/60/120 GPUs) and share with finance (2026-03-13).
- Ops oncall: instrument additional metrics for cold-start traces (trace id + stage timings) (2026-03-12).

Notes to self / talking points
- Emphasize that extra reservation reduces OOM/queueing for high-throughput tails and lowers per-token costs by enabling better batching.
- Be explicit about canary: add +10 GPUs to east/day-1, monitor 95th pct latency and failed allocations for 72 hours before committing remainder.
- Have fallback: if commit delayed, prioritize prewarm + burst cap increase only.

Draft email / ask to execs (short)
Subject: Proposal – +60 GPUs reserved to cover near-term Dedicated demand
Body: Quick ask: monitoring shows 95th pct utilization at 88% during peak and projected demand suggests we need +60 A100-eq GPUs in April to avoid degraded latency for reserved customers. Recommend approval for +60 reserve + temporary burst cap increase to 80 per region for 6 weeks while we stabilize prewarm pipelines. Will follow with cost sensitivity.

Links/refs
- JIRA-ENG-3421 (onboarding ticket for BigRetail co)
- confluence://redwood/dedicated-capacity-playbook (current playbook + autoscale RFC)
- infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/678 (image layering work)
- Slack thread: #eng-dedicated thread-2391 (customer spike logs)

End notes: Clean up numbers + attach charts (utilization by region, 7d/30d growth) before sending to Ryan/Jenna.
